text.title: Agency Pricing Tiers Worked Example
text.summary: One complete good / better / best ladder for a paid-search agency at 3,000 / 5,000 / 8,000 EUR a month with costed tiers, best at 54.5 percent margin, nested deliverables, conversion tracking as the fence, a scope-up procedure and best-first presentation, with a note on each non-obvious value; then the ladder as it is usually built and what the validator prints.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: A paid-search agency sells one 5,000 EUR a month engagement to e-commerce SMEs and loses both the anchor above it and the upsell path. Loaded hourly cost is 90 EUR; ad-platform tooling is passed through at cost. The ICP buys measurable ROAS, which needs conversion tracking.

example.title: 3,000 / 5,000 / 8,000 EUR ladder
example.note: Three tiers, no fourth priced row; a custom scope lives outside the table (r-exactly-three-priced-tiers). Margins are computed, not asserted: good is 3,000 - (20 x 90 + 200) = 1,000 (33.3 percent), better 5,000 - (28 x 90 + 300) = 2,180 (43.6 percent), best 8,000 - (36 x 90 + 400) = 4,360 (54.5 percent), so best leads on both, because it adds 8 senior hours while its price adds 3,000 (r-best-tier-highest-margin). 5,000 / 3,000 = 1.67 and 8,000 / 5,000 = 1.6, the 3 / 5 / 8 shape exactly, so no gap justification is needed (r-price-gaps-follow-3-5-8). Every good deliverable is in better with more campaigns and a faster report, and every better deliverable is in best; the weekly call keeps quantity 4 and turnaround 7 rather than being swapped for something else (r-tiers-are-strict-supersets). Conversion tracking is the fence: an e-commerce buyer who wants ROAS cannot stay on good, and better holds the complete core offer, so it is the default recommendation (r-good-tier-fenced-middle-tier-complete). The scope-up names the trigger, the pro-rated price difference, the account director as approver and written confirmation; goodwill extras are not permitted (r-scope-up-procedure-documented). Concessions remove a named deliverable or quantity; the three prices are the same for every client (r-discount-by-scope-not-price). The rate sheet lists best first with all three prices visible (r-present-best-first).

example.title: the same agency's ladder as usually built
example.note: What the validator prints: `presentation.order` starts with good and `prices_visible` is false (r-present-best-first); `scope_up.free_goodwill_allowed` is true (r-scope-up-procedure-documented); `concessions.published_prices_vary_by_client` is true (r-discount-by-scope-not-price); the only step's `exit_criterion` is "shipped" (r-price-gaps-follow-3-5-8). Once those are fixed the cross-field checks add: best's margin is 15,000 - (140 x 90 + 400) = 2,000 at 13.3 percent, the lowest of the three, because 140 hours of senior time were packed in (best-tier-lowest-margin); the prices are 5 / 10 / 15, so better / good is 2.0 and best / better 1.5, outside the 3 / 5 / 8 band with no justification (equal-price-steps); conversion tracking sits in good but not in better, and social campaigns in better but not in best, so the tiers swap instead of nesting (tiers-swap-instead-of-nest); and the fence names a deliverable that good already has, so nothing pushes a buyer to the middle. What the reviewer sees: a ladder where the top tier sells and loses money and the middle tier has no reason to exist.
